scope: Existing C14 raw state time series, final metrics, closed379-cursor context aggregate, SQLite schema/query plans and frozen relevant source only. No source-body replay or performance rerun.

observedRates.unitPolicy: MB=1000000 bytes; MiB=1048576 bytes. Rates measure committed historical offsets, not disk throughput or partially discarded physical bytes.

supportedFindings.finding: The later throughput decline combines smaller committed work per collector iteration and longer wall intervals.
supportedFindings.causalLimit: This decomposition does not identify CPU, I/O, locks or individual phase time.

supportedFindings.finding: 250ms is checked inside reader scheduling/line boundaries, not an upper bound for whole Core scan or collector cycle.
supportedFindings.causalLimit: Frozen desktop starts this timer before Core lock acquisition and records after scan/report conversion while taking metrics lock. The value includes those waits/work; it excludes following notifications and Condvar wait. No per-phase timings or contended boolean were persisted.

supportedFindings.finding: Oversized partial-line physical progress can fail the line-count progress gate.
supportedFindings.mechanism: The incomplete oversized branch advances discard_offset and persists an issue, then breaks before report.lines increment and bytes+=read. It returns0 bytes if no earlier complete line. If no other complete lines were processed, desktop selects the2s fallback despite physical discard progress. Completed oversized/invalid lines increment report.issues and also select2s fallback; the25ms fast yield additionally requires no Core contention.
supportedFindings.causalLimit: Only one of370 observed adjacent collector intervals had unchanged historical committed bytes, and all closed historical/live discard offsets are0. This mechanism is real but is not established as the dominant delay in this run; historical-offset rates can hide transient discard progress.

supportedFindings.finding: Completed files are revisited for safety and count against scheduling time; current metadata does not show huge completed-file anchor volume.
supportedFindings.mechanism: Each source scan rediscover/sorts files; every visited completed file opens shared handle, reads/hash prefix, queries stored state and revalidates the last committed line anchor before fast continue. same_anchor has a4MiB read bound but no250ms/deadline/cancel argument. Completed files still rotate with unfinished files.
supportedFindings.causalLimit: Closed276/379 files are complete; their last-line length proxy totals434635bytes and max11653bytes. Per-file metadata/SQL/anchor elapsed and visit mix were not recorded, so a dominant completed-file revalidation bottleneck is not proven.

supportedFindings.finding: Retention performs repeated table work outside the250ms reader phase; five delete predicates compile to full scans.
supportedFindings.causalLimit: These plans prove an existing per-batch cost path, not its share of the measured4s collector cost. No retention-phase timing was captured.

ruledOutOrUnproven.budgetFullLoadExplanation: budgets table is empty; evaluate_budgets returns before budget_views/load. That particular full-load budget path did not run here.

separateResourceFailure: The671.9375MiB threshold failure already has exact executable attribution in its independent receipt. This diagnostic neither reattributes that failure to reader throughput nor changes it.
limitations: No source log bodies were read, no fullDB hash/integrity rerun, no Core call, build, model/app-server process, UI or new performance run.
Closed cursors include normal app continuation after the threshold observer stopped; they are not a time series of per-file work.
The state stream proves slowing committed progress; final metrics provide one aggregate cost sample, not historical per-scan phase profiles.
No600MiB/350MiB/3600s/CPU/startup/increment gate or existing oracle was changed. No speed improvement or whole-M4 qualification is claimed.
